sample_size.excerpt: The current analysis is based on those men responding to questions on early life rye bread consumption (n = 2,258), midlife rye bread consumption (n = 2,260), early life oatmeal consumption (n = 2,255), midlife oatmeal consumption (n = 2,259) and midlife whole wheat bread consumption (n =2,255).

effect_size.excerpt: ≤4 times/ week) was not associated with risk of prostate cancer diagnosis (OR = 0.99, 95% CI: 0.77-1.27), nor statistically significant with advanced prostate cancer (OR = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.37-1.20). High intake of oatmeal in midlife was not associated with prostate cancer risk and neither was current intake for either total prostate cancer (HR = 1.06, 95% CI: 0.74-1.52) nor advanced disease (HR = 0.99, 95% CI: 0.44-2.23).
